questions.q: Which of the following is true?
options: Human memory involves the ability to only preserve information
Human memory involves the ability to only recover information
Human memory involves the ability to neither preserve nor recover information
Human memory involves the ability to both preserve and recover information
questions.explanation: Human memory involves encoding and storing (preserving) information and also retrieving (recovering) it when needed. Memory without either part would be useless.

questions.q: ____ refers to connections between the nerve cells
questions.explanation: Synapses are the junctions where one nerve cell communicates with another. Neurons are the nerve cells themselves, not the connections between them.

questions.q: In order to create a new memory, information must be changed into ____
questions.explanation: Encoding, the first stage of memory formation, transforms incoming information into a usable form that can be stored as a new memory.

questions.q: The memory ____ process allows us to bring stored memories into conscious awareness.
questions.explanation: Retrieval is the process of bringing stored information back into conscious awareness. Encoding puts information in, storage keeps it, and forgetting is the failure of retrieval or storage.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a major domain of cognition?
questions.explanation: Major cognitive domains include attention, memory, perception, judgment/reasoning, language and intelligence. Aggression is a behavior or emotional disposition, not a domain of cognition.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an assumption of the information processing view?
options: Information is processed in steps or stages
There are limits on how much information can be processed
The human information processing system is interactive
Information processing is analogous to computer processing
questions.explanation: The keyed answer treats the limited-capacity idea as not being an assumption of the information processing view.
questions.flag: Likely wrong key: limited capacity (e.g., 7 plus or minus 2 items in short-term memory) is a core assumption of the information processing view, and 2026 week03 states this as True. The computer analogy is more of a metaphor than an assumption and is probably the intended answer.

questions.q: ____ refers to rote rehearsal of repetition
questions.explanation: Maintenance rehearsal is simple rote repetition that keeps information active in short-term memory. Elaborative rehearsal links information to existing knowledge and is more effective for long-term retention.

questions.q: ____ presentations can enhance working memory capacity
questions.explanation: Presenting information through multiple modes (e.g., visual and auditory) spreads load across separate working-memory subsystems (visuo-spatial sketchpad and phonological loop), effectively increasing capacity (the modality effect).

questions.q: Episodic and semantic memories are categorized under ____ memory
questions.explanation: Declarative (explicit) memory includes episodic memory for personal events and semantic memory for facts and general knowledge. Procedural memory is a non-declarative memory for skills.

questions.q: According to the neural network model, memory capacity depends on ____
options: spatial and temporal correlations between memories
questions.explanation: In neural network models, how many memories can be stored depends on synaptic complexity, the sparseness of representations, and the spatial and temporal correlations among stored memories, so all options apply.
